event.marcus_heart2.0.text: Take the far end, [player]. Don't level it. Don't fix it. Just hold.
event.marcus_heart2.0.why: the test is explicit now: no helping, only steadiness

event.marcus_heart2.1.text: Measure once. Twice. ...Three times, my father said. Level as a lake in August.
event.marcus_heart2.1.why: August makes the lake still and specific

event.marcus_heart2.3.text: Most hands drift after a minute. Yours didn't. I was counting.
event.marcus_heart2.3.why: reveals he was quietly timing an audition

event.marcus_heart2.2.text: Here. Leftovers from good jobs. Every one an inch short of the hall roof. I keep checking.
event.marcus_heart2.2.why: an inch short, and he keeps checking; the roof thread sharpened

event.marcus_heart5.0.text: I carved this the winter I was nine. A barn, about the size of a fist.
event.marcus_heart5.0.why: a whole winter at nine; the patience started early

event.marcus_heart5.1.text: Silly, perhaps. The doors don't open. I glued them in a hurry and the hurry won. I want you to have it.
event.marcus_heart5.1.why: his one rushed job, named as a defeat

event.marcus_heart5.4.text: Edmund had a door like that. The cellar. I offered to oil the hinge every spring. He always said next spring.
event.marcus_heart5.4.why: 'next spring' mirrors Marcus's own 'nearly'; cozy-safe, unexplained

event.marcus_heart5.3.text: My father said fast work stays wrong. He kept that barn on his shelf anyway. Eye level.
event.marcus_heart5.3.why: eye level is the father's pride, unstated

event.marcus_heart5.2.text: The bag is for your fields. Crops are the one thing I allow to hurry.
event.marcus_heart5.2.why: one idea; 'hurry' lands as the gift

event.story_pie_payoff.intro.text: [player]. A word, quietly. You walk past the clinic most days, don't you?
event.story_pie_payoff.intro.why: reconnaissance, not a request; he has been watching routes

dlg.story.pie.talk.1.text: You can say no. The pie and I will just stand here. We're patient.

dlg.story.whistler.marcus.0.text: A family tune. Grandfather hit one note wrong at my father's wedding. We've kept it wrong ever since.
dlg.story.whistler.marcus.0.why: the wedding dates the mistake; kept wrong on purpose

event.story_pumpkin_marcus.intro.text: Caught. It's a practice lantern. I measured the face twice. I asked whose pumpkin zero times.

event.marcus_heart8.intro.text: Come in. You've seen my worst joint, the glued doors. Time you saw the roof plan. Nobody has.
event.marcus_heart8.intro.why: heart5 callback; the plan outranks the carving as a confession

dlg.marcus.roof.1.text: Six winters of nearly. The village runs a pool on me. ...What would you do?
dlg.marcus.roof.1.why: he knows about the pool; the shame said flatly

event.marcus_birthday.intro.text: My birthday. Every year I plane one plank for it, slow, no customer waiting. Sit, if you like.
event.marcus_birthday.intro.why: the one job he does for nobody; slow is the celebration

event.overheard_bram_marcus_2.l4.text: Then it's right. A handle should vanish in the hand.
event.overheard_bram_marcus_2.l4.why: drops the repeated 'Good.' opener; verdict, then proverb

threads.marcus_heart2: Marcus keeps measuring leftover wood against the hall roof and finding every piece an inch short.
threads.marcus_heart5: Edmund's cellar door, the hinge Marcus was never allowed to oil, and why Edmund always said next spring.
threads.story_pie_payoff: Two bakers are now baking replies at each other; the feud has become a correspondence.
threads.story_whistler_marcus: Wednesdays on the bench Marcus whistles the family's wrong note, and Bram pretends not to hear.
threads.story_pumpkin_marcus: Marcus owes Tilda an exactly measured pie, and next year he asks first. Probably.
threads.marcus_heart8: The roof has moved for the first time in six winters; the village pool is suddenly in danger.
threads.marcus_birthday: One plank a year, planed slow for no customer; nobody has asked what he is saving them for.
threads.overheard_bram_marcus_1: Wednesday, same bench: the standing lunch between the forge and the shop.
threads.overheard_bram_marcus_2: Bram's hammer now wears a handle measured to a grip he never offered.
threads.overheard_bram_marcus_3: A nail-straightness contest is set for Wednesday, and lunch rides on it.
threads.overheard_marcus_odalys_1: Dr. Penn keeps a window-side ledger of who lifts what, and Marcus is in it.
threads.overheard_marcus_odalys_3: Saturdays: Marcus is building Dr. Penn a chair so she takes her own advice.

notes: hall_dance .0 and .11 kept unchanged: they are the payoff of 'Measure twice' and 'nearly'; please keep Wren's pool line after mine so 'Finished' lands first.
marcus_heart8 n1 now names the roof pool; consistent with Wren closing it at hall_dance ('six winters of coins').
marcus_heart5 plays the Edmund line (.4) before the father line (.3); kept as ordered, but the father line would land better before Edmund if reordering is ever allowed.
Pie dialogue narrations r0-r2 describe off-screen sighs and bites; accepted shape from the card, flagged in case the engine narration rule applies inside dialogue graphs.
